narrative:
The assessment estimated a 55% probability that you would represent a bad credit risk, which is why your application was declined. This means the information provided was judged to lean more toward repayment difficulty than toward reliable repayment, so the loan was not approved.

The strongest factor was your checking account status. Your account is recorded as overdrawn (below 0 DM), a situation seen for only about 12.6% of approved applicants, and this pushed the decision toward bad credit. The second most influential factor was the amount requested. You asked for 4,006 DM, above the approved average of about 3,020 DM, but this factor actually worked in your favour and reduced the estimated risk. The third factor was the loan purpose. A new car request was the third strongest influence and pushed toward bad credit; it is also less common among approved applicants than borrowing for radio/TV or furniture.

To improve a future application, focus first on bringing your checking account into a non-overdrawn position and keeping it there. Consider requesting a smaller amount, adding a guarantor or co-applicant if possible, and building savings before reapplying. You may also ask the lender what specific changes would strengthen a new application.
